steps.say: In this lesion the two great arteries leave the wrong ventricles, so oxygenated and deoxygenated blood run on separate loops that never meet.
steps.tx: Connections show **ventriculoarterial discordance with parallel circulation**. D transposition features ventriculoarterial discordance where the aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the left ventricle, creating two parallel, independent circulations that cannot sustain life without mixing between them, and the infant depends entirely on prompt prostaglandin support after delivery.

vis.caption: Cyanotic congenital cardiac anomalies and classic pulmonary vascular patterns on radiography. Image: Dong Soo Kim.
vis.alt: Radiological and anatomical comparison of cyanotic heart defects.

steps.say: A baby with this anatomy survives only through holes that let the two circuits trade blood, which is why the ductus must never be allowed to close.
steps.tx: Survival requires **intercirculatory mixing at an obligatory mixing site**. Survival requires communication between the circuits via a patent ductus arteriosus, atrial septal defect, or ventricular septal defect, so prostaglandin infusion is started immediately and oxygen alone is never relied upon to improve saturation, because supplemental oxygen cannot bridge two circuits that never meet.

rows: Improves mixing and delays LV regression

steps.say: The chest film shows an egg balanced on a string, a silhouette produced by the abnormally stacked great vessels.
steps.tx: Radiography demonstrates the **egg-on-a-string appearance (egg on a string sign)**. Chest radiograph classically demonstrates an egg on a string cardiac silhouette due to a narrow superior mediastinal shadow from anteroposterior great vessel alignment and thymic involution, with increased pulmonary vascular markings from torrential pulmonary flow.

left.title: Egg (Cardiac Shadow)
points: Ovoid enlarged heart from volume loaded ventricles
Pulmonary plethora with engorged vascular markings
Right heart border formed by the right sided left atrium

right.title: String (Mediastinum)
points: Narrow pedicle from anteroposterior vessel stacking
Absent thymic shadow from stress involution

steps.say: At the bedside, often under echo guidance alone, a balloon catheter can tear a generous hole in the atrial septum within minutes.
steps.tx: Stabilization uses the **Rashkind septostomy**. Balloon atrial septostomy (the Rashkind procedure) is performed percutaneously or at the bedside under echocardiographic guidance to create a large unrestrictive interatrial communication, rapidly improving mixing and saturation in a crashing neonate, and the torn septum stays open reliably until the arterial switch is performed.

nodes.label: Umbilical or femoral venous access with balloon catheter to right atrium
Balloon advanced across foramen ovale into the left atrium
Inflated balloon jerked back to tear the septum primum
Confirm unrestrictive atrial shunt with saturation rise on echo

steps.say: The modern cure physically swaps the arteries back to their correct ventricles, carrying the tiny coronary buttons along with them.
steps.tx: Correction is the **arterial switch operation**. The arterial switch operation (the Jatene procedure) is the definitive anatomical correction of choice, transecting and switching the great vessels with coronary artery reimplantation, which restores the left ventricle as the systemic pump, and long term outcomes now rival those of simpler arterial repairs.

rows: Aorta and pulmonary artery divided above sinuses
Excised cuffs reimplanted into neo aorta
Pulmonary bifurcation draped anterior to aorta
Avoids compression of the translocated vessels

steps.say: Timing is everything: leave the left ventricle pumping to low resistance lungs for a month and it becomes too weak to face the body.
steps.tx: Timing follows the **Jatene procedure window (left ventricular preparedness)**. The arterial switch operation must be performed within the first **2-3 weeks** of life in intact ventricular septum cases, before left ventricular mass regresses from pumping against low pulmonary resistance, after which the ventricle cannot sustain systemic afterload.

left.title: Early Switch (<3 Weeks)
points: Left ventricle still thick from fetal systemic workload
Single stage anatomical correction with excellent survival
Standard pathway for intact septum transposition

right.title: Late Presentation
points: Regressed left ventricle fails against sudden systemic load
Needs rapid two stage retraining with pulmonary banding
Ventricular septal defect cases stay prepared longer

steps.say: A rarer cousin flips both the atria and the arteries, leaving the right ventricle to do the heavy lifelong work for the body.
steps.tx: The related entity is **congenitally corrected transposition**. Congenitally corrected transposition (L-TGA, ccTGA) features both atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, where the systemic ventricle is the morphologic right ventricle, an arrangement that stays compensated for decades before systemic ventricular failure appears in adult life.

nodes.label: Right atrium connects through mitral valve to left ventricle
Left ventricle ejects into the pulmonary artery normally
Left atrium connects through tricuspid valve to right ventricle
Morphologic right ventricle sustains the systemic circulation

steps.say: Even without surgery, this corrected form carries a slow electrical price: the conduction bundle fails a little more with every passing year.
steps.tx: Follow up anticipates **progressive heart block in L-TGA**. Spontaneous complete atrioventricular block develops at a rate of approximately **2 percent per year** throughout life in congenitally corrected transposition due to an elongated, abnormal conduction bundle, mandating lifelong Holter surveillance and a low threshold for pacing.
